question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity Vector at a Point in Time Given the Acceleration Vector
question.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨12(1+2t)^{3},9(1-3t)^{2}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨1,6⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=1.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨12(1+2t)^{3},9(1-3t)^{2}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 12(1+2t)^{3}\,\text{d}t,\int 9(1-3t)^{2}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2}(1+2t)^{4}+{C}_{1},\,-(1-3t)^{3}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(0)=⟨1,6⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨\frac{3}{2}(1+2(0))^{4}+{C}_{1},\,-(1-3(0))^{3}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,6⟩ & =⟨\frac{3}{2}+{C}_{1},\,-1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}$ and ${C}_{2}=7.$ Therefore, the velocity is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨\frac{3}{2}(1+2t)^{4}-\frac{1}{2},\,-(1-3t)^{3}+7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at time $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨\frac{3}{2}(1+2(1))^{4}-\frac{1}{2},\,-(1-3(1))^{3}+7⟩ \\  & =⟨121,15⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
